title: AnnoAudit confirmatory-eligibility criteria for neuron-level inference in public single-cell atlases
scope: Decides whether a public single-cell atlas can support a confirmatory, neuron-level (or other cell-type-level) claim about a gene's temporal dynamics, on the basis of the deposited count matrix and the declared biological replicates.
not_in_scope: Judging the correctness of a depositing laboratory's cell-type annotation
Any claim about resources whose matrices were not examined
Choosing a marker panel appropriate for a non-neuronal cell type (the criteria below are written for excitatory neurons; the neuronal-signal clause must be re-derived for other lineages)

criteria.name: neuronal-signal sufficiency
criteria.statement: At least 1% of all cells in the library reach >= 10 counts for a strict canonical neuronal gene.
criteria.rationale: The count matrix must contain neuronal signal for a neuron-level analysis to mean anything. Computed on the whole library and without reference to any label, so that ambient contamination of a labelled subset cannot influence it.

criteria.name: replicate adequacy
criteria.statement: At least 100 marker-confirmed excitatory neurons per biological replicate, and at least two biological replicates per group.
criteria.rationale: Twice the ~50 cells per sample-cell-type combination at which aggregate profiles become noisy (muscat). We take twice that margin because the design has only three replicates per group. This is the criterion that carries the decision: applied alone it selects only the atlas that passes, at every threshold examined, and every criterion combination that includes it gives the same verdict.

criteria.name: depth comparability
criteria.statement: The ratio of the maximum to the minimum group median UMI count is no greater than 1.5.
criteria.rationale: Depth differences generate apparent detection-rate differences for sparsely expressed transcripts, so a comparison across groups of unequal depth is not interpretable without depth matching. In the atlas set examined here this criterion has limited discriminating power (three of five atlases pass), although it does independently reject one of them (GSE247339, max/min group median UMI ratio 1.61). It is retained because it is a precondition for the depth-matched comparison, not because it excludes anything.

criteria.name: definition-stability
criteria.statement: The direction of the effect is concordant across all five pre-specified nested excitatory-neuron definitions (D1-D5).
criteria.rationale: Applied to the result rather than to the dataset. Because the five nested definitions share one marker, agreement among them is partly tautological; three structurally independent definitions (N1-N3) were added afterwards as corroboration and are reported separately from this criterion.

combination.statement: A dataset is eligible only if it satisfies every criterion. Criteria are conjoined, not interchangeable: in the atlas set examined, C1 alone would admit the atlas with the highest ambient contamination, and C3 alone admits three of the five atlases assessed.
combination.alternatives_examined: Every single criterion and every two-criterion combination was tested at three neuronal-signal thresholds. All combinations containing C2 select the same single atlas at every threshold; no combination without C2 is stable. Those alternative combinations were not adopted.

threshold_robustness.result: verdict unchanged for the adopted combination at all three thresholds

excitatory_definitions.note: All definitions are applied to the deposited count matrix with the gene symbols as written by the depositor; symbol case is matched case-insensitively. 'pan-neuronal detected' means max(count) > 0 over the pan-neuronal set; 'microglia not dominant' means max(microglial count) <= max(pan-neuronal count).

D4.rule: Slc17a7 >= 3 AND pan-neuronal detected AND microglia not dominant

D5.rule: Slc17a7 >= 5 AND pan-neuronal detected AND microglia not dominant

independent.added: after the nested family had shown 15/15 concordance, as a check on whether that concordance was an artefact of the shared marker
independent.evidential_weight: independent corroboration, not a pre-specified criterion

N1.rule: Snap25 >= 10 AND pan-neuronal detected AND microglia not dominant

N2.rule: Slc17a7 >= 3 AND Neurod6 > 0 AND microglia not dominant

N3.rule: Slc17a7 >= 1 AND Camk2a > 0 AND pan-neuronal detected AND microglia not dominant AND Gad1 == 0 AND Gad2 == 0

reporting_requirements: State the failure mode for every excluded dataset, not only that it was excluded
State whether the failure mode is recoverable in principle, and what remedy it would require
Report which criterion or criteria carry the decision, so that a reader applying the rule to a new dataset knows what to check first
Report the biological replicate identity and count for each group; the replicate, not the cell, is the unit of analysis
provenance_note: These criteria are written for datasets whose deposited matrices are accompanied by per-cell gene counts and for which the biological replicate of each cell can be stated. They carry no claim about the annotations of any depositing laboratory, and they should not be read as evaluating the correctness of any external cell-type annotation.
